dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

candidate.prototype: R-3m four-site layered Lu-Ta-N2 ordered phase; two N sites form a common orbit, Lu and Ta occupy distinct cation sheets
candidate.prototype_evidence: R-3m four-site layered Lu-Ta-N2 ordered phase; two N sites form a common orbit, Lu and Ta occupy distinct cation sheets
candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: Ta SOC and Lu electronic-shell treatment, cation order versus competing nitrides, and layered shear are case-specific risks. Full fine stress reaches .242 GPa and fine force .01729 eV/A; coarse force 2.19e-5 eV/A/P=.001 GPa and the nonnegative finite path/positive Gamma optical subspace support a bounded near-ambient local phase. No claim of global hull or experimentally realized phase.
candidate.ambient_scope: Coarse/fine SCF both converge; complete source forces/stress, positive Gamma optical compression and no signed negative finite-path value support this model near ambient. All listed q outputs end JOBDONE/response convergence with zero routine errors. This is finite-grid local/metastable evidence, not exhaustive thermodynamic or all-irrep certification.
candidate.route_response: Replace Y by Lu in the frozen YTaN2 analogue. Volume decreases 4.316116%; Lu-N versus Y-N nearest distance decreases .0744086 A while Ta-N increases .00273149 A. Same ecut/smearing/degauss/pseudo-family directory and 4x4x4/13-q grid give all-ten lambda gains 45.878–51.321%, separate Eli mu=.1 12.416→15.539 K. The opposite changes in cation-N and Ta-N distances distinguish local reconstruction from a uniform-volume description.
candidate.next_action: Compare YTaN2/LuTaN2 at a common volume and with a consistent SOC treatment or one matched layer-shear/metal-N mode. Favorable: the 45–51% source advantage survives and the layer branch stays positive; adverse: SOC/order changes remove the advantage or a competing nitride path destabilizes the phase.

seven_criteria.identity: Raw CIF, literal coarse/fine crystal input and Gamma header agree by complete ordered species/site periodic association; exact natural-isotope discrete computational occupancy is export convention, experimental occupancy/P/T unknown. Source model configured neutral scalar spin1/noSOC by exact-version defaults plus literal omission; magnetic ground state and binary build not certified.
seven_criteria.quantitative_route_response: Replace Y by Lu in the frozen YTaN2 analogue. Volume decreases 4.316116%; Lu-N versus Y-N nearest distance decreases .0744086 A while Ta-N increases .00273149 A. Same ecut/smearing/degauss/pseudo-family directory and 4x4x4/13-q grid give all-ten lambda gains 45.878–51.321%, separate Eli mu=.1 12.416→15.539 K. The opposite changes in cation-N and Ta-N distances distinguish local reconstruction from a uniform-volume description.
seven_criteria.pairing_relevance: Direct exact-source lambda has the favorable sign at all ten matched sigma tokens, independently accompanied by the separate mu=.1 Eli table. Finite-grid broadening sensitivity is preserved; differing PP/cutoff/version are model confounds where shown. Sigma units, physical error bar, fullBZ convergence and experimental Tc remain unknown.
seven_criteria.ambient_feasibility: Coarse/fine SCF both converge; complete source forces/stress, positive Gamma optical compression and no signed negative finite-path value support this model near ambient. All listed q outputs end JOBDONE/response convergence with zero routine errors. This is finite-grid local/metastable evidence, not exhaustive thermodynamic or all-irrep certification.
seven_criteria.competition_and_coherence: Ta SOC and Lu electronic-shell treatment, cation order versus competing nitrides, and layered shear are case-specific risks. Full fine stress reaches .242 GPa and fine force .01729 eV/A; coarse force 2.19e-5 eV/A/P=.001 GPa and the nonnegative finite path/positive Gamma optical subspace support a bounded near-ambient local phase. No claim of global hull or experimentally realized phase.
seven_criteria.novelty: 2026-10-07 LuTaN2/TaLuN2 exact search found no experimental SC benchmark. Related CaM N2 layered nitrides have known superconducting phases, but they are different cations/chemistry and do not make this exact Lu/Ta ordered phase a benchmark. MC2023 source prediction remains prior.
seven_criteria.decision: Compare YTaN2/LuTaN2 at a common volume and with a consistent SOC treatment or one matched layer-shear/metal-N mode. Favorable: the 45–51% source advantage survives and the layer branch stays positive; adverse: SOC/order changes remove the advantage or a competing nitride path destabilizes the phase.
